children.description: Torreya — a genus of pinopsidas.

children.name: Torreya californica
children.description: Torreya californica is a species of conifer endemic to California, occurring in the Pacific Coast Ranges and the foothills of the Sierra Nevada.

children.name: Torreya dapanshanica
children.description: The native range of this species is China (Zhejiang). It is a tree and grows primarily in the temperate biome.

children.name: Torreya fargesii
children.description: Torreya fargesii (Farges nutmeg tree, ) is a species of conifer in the family Taxaceae.

children.name: Torreya grandis
children.description: Torreya grandis ( ) is a species of conifer in either the family Taxaceae, or Cephalotaxaceae.

children.name: Torreya jackii
children.description: Torreya jackii ( ) is a species of conifer in the family Taxaceae.

children.name: Torreya nucifera
children.description: Torreya nucifera is a slow-growing, coniferous tree native to southern Japan and to South Korea's Jeju Island.

children.name: Torreya taxifolia
children.description: Torreya taxifolia, commonly known as Florida torreya or stinking-cedar, but also sometimes as Florida nutmeg or gopher wood, is an endangered subcanopy tree of the yew family, Taxaceae.

children.name: Taxus
children.description: Taxus — a genus of pinopsidas.

children.name: Taxus baccata
children.description: Taxus baccata is an Old World species of evergreen tree in the family Taxaceae.

children.name: Taxus brevifolia
children.description: Taxus brevifolia, the Pacific yew or western yew, is a species of tree in the yew family Taxaceae native to the Pacific Northwest of North America.

children.name: Taxus calcicola
children.description: The native range of this species is China (SE. Yunnan, Guizhou) to N. Vietnam. It is a tree and grows primarily in the temperate biome.

children.name: Taxus canadensis
children.description: Taxus canadensis, the Canada yew or Canadian yew, is a conifer native to central and eastern North America, thriving in swampy woods, ravines, riverbanks and on lake shores.

children.name: Taxus chinensis
children.description: Taxus chinensis is a species of yew.

children.name: Taxus contorta
children.description: Taxus contorta, synonym Taxus fuana, commonly known as the West Himalayan yew, is a species of tree in the genus Taxus.

children.name: Taxus cuspidata
children.description: Taxus cuspidata, the Japanese yew or spreading yew, is a member of the genus Taxus, native to Japan, Korea, northeast China and the extreme southeast of Russia.

children.name: Taxus floridana
children.description: Taxus floridana, the Florida yew, is a species of yew, endemic to a small area of the Apalachicola River.

children.name: Taxus florinii
children.description: The native range of this species is China (SW. Sichuan, NW. Yunnan). It is a tree and grows primarily in the temperate biome.

children.name: Taxus globosa
children.description: Taxus globosa, the Mexican yew, is an evergreen shrub and one of the eight species of yew.

children.name: Taxus mairei
children.description: Taxus mairei, Maire's yew, is a species of conifer in the yew family Taxaceae, native to Nepal, Assam, central and southern China, Hainan, Taiwan and Vietnam.

children.name: Taxus qinlingensis
children.description: The native range of this species is China (Gansu, Shanxi, Henan). It is a tree and grows primarily in the temperate biome.

children.name: Taxus wallichiana
children.description: Taxus wallichiana, the Himalayan yew, is a species of yew, native to the Himalaya and parts of south-east Asia.
